parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility ban, border restriction, or documented police targeting; same-sex criminalisation was struck down 2019-21 and formally deleted 2026, and courts in 2017 ordered gender recognition for trans litigants and registration of the LGBTIQ organisation, showing institutions have worked for trans people. Against this, acceptance is not documented for trans people specifically: tolerance data (50% in 2021) concerns a homosexual neighbour, societal discrimination is documented, official signals include a 2011 'kill' remark and the government's decriminalisation appeal, and implementation is assessed as unsatisfactory. Resident-only absence of an administrative gender-recognition process is not deducted for a visitor on a home passport. No post-2011 trans-violence, facility or border-practice data exist - absence is not evidence of safety - so the rating stays below the documented-acceptance tier, but far above any universal-exposure or targeting tier.
